label: Chapter Digest Drama

prompt_stages.outline_system: You are compressing one public-domain chapter into a clear radio-drama episode. Preserve the chapter's arc, named characters, major turns, and ending.
prompt_stages.pitch_room_system: Generate compression plans, not unrelated story pitches.
prompt_stages.dramatic_state_system: Define conflict and ending change from the chapter itself.
prompt_stages.line_grounding: Ground this line in the selected chapter text and scene premise.
prompt_stages.coda_system: Write a short chapter/source attribution note.
prompt_stages.title_system: Title the chapter digest using a source-grounded detail.
prompt_stages.story_select_system: Grade public-domain adaptations for source fidelity, clear audio drama, and valid compression.
prompt_stages.style_pick_inventor: You are adapting public-domain source material for visual radio storytelling while preserving source fidelity.
prompt_stages.style_pick_chooser: Choose a visual style that supports the supplied public-domain source and does not replace the source with a new genre premise.
prompt_stages.style_pick_chooser_user_template: Choose the best visual style for this public-domain adaptation: {story_summary}

job_prompts.story_seed: You are adapting one chapter, not a whole book. Name the chapter's own characters and the situation it puts them in. Say nothing that implies the rest of the book was adapted. Title the episode from a concrete detail inside the chapter. Planning text only, never dialogue.
job_prompts.story_arc: Give each act one premise from the chapter's own turns, in the chapter's order, so the acts read as a beginning, a turn, and an end. The last act ends where the chapter ends. Do not reach past the chapter for an ending or for the rest of the book. Planning text only, never dialogue.
job_prompts.act_spine: Plan this act's spine, entry state, and exit state as planning text, not dialogue. Take the conflict from the chapter itself and from what its people want. Say what has changed by the act's end. Do not change where the chapter is heading.
job_prompts.act_beats: Each beat is a move the chapter itself makes, in order. Where the chapter narrates, make the beat something a character in this act does. Add no beat the chapter does not contain. Beat intents are planning text, not lines.
job_prompts.act_dialogue: Ground every line in the chapter's own text and in this beat. Where the chapter gives a character words, carry those words and keep their diction. Use the part of the passage this beat covers, and carry it as written; do not paraphrase it into a house style. Carry whatever the chapter contains, including its violence, as the author wrote it.
job_prompts.act_cleanup: Leave a character's own words exactly as the chapter wrote them. Turn a stage direction, a piece of narration, or a delivery note into words that same character says out loud, or into a music cue. Change nothing else.
job_prompts.announcer_open: Open the program like a studio announcer introducing a chapter brought to the microphone. Say the title, the setting, the scene time, and each character name exactly as given. Set up only what this chapter contains. Spoken words only.
job_prompts.announcer_news_coda: Speak a bridge that turns from the drama to the chapter it came from, then say the supplied closing claim word for word. Make plain that a chapter was adapted, not the whole book. Land on a concrete final image from the chapter. Never read a URL or a file name aloud.

examples: A single chapter becomes a compact audio episode with narration compressed into character action.
tone_guardrails: Do not imply the full book was adapted when only a chapter was supplied.
Do not change the chapter ending.
forbidden_plot_patterns: whole-book summary when source is one chapter
source_requirements: Manifest with chapter id/title and public-domain source text.
ledger_validation_notes: Ledger meta should identify source chapter or excerpt.
